changes: Revalidates every unattended Automation target against the live library and physical media immediately before NZB retrieval/submission, suppressing stale missing/upgrade grabs after the target has already changed.

Recovers trustworthy existing-media quality from the live record, fingerprint cache, filename, or conservative media probe and treats unknown existing quality as protected rather than as permission to overwrite.

Enforces a fail-closed no-downgrade gate immediately before Smart Import commit: an incoming file may replace an existing library file only when it is provably strictly better; otherwise the existing file is kept.
Adds optimistic concurrency to long library scans so scan results captured before a Smart Import cannot overwrite newer per-episode or movie file state at commit time.
Adds Automation target-integrity diagnostics for stale grabs suppressed, scan merge conflicts, downgrades blocked, recovered existing quality, and last integrity event time.
regression_guards: Manual Interactive Search and one-time Discover media grabs remain user-controlled; the stale-target suppression gate applies only to unattended automatic Automation grabs.
A genuinely missing target may still use an allowed fallback quality such as 720p when that profile permits it; the new guard blocks only stale or unsafe replacement of existing media.
Legitimate quality upgrades remain allowed only when the incoming quality is provably better than the current physical library file.
Long library scans still reconcile unchanged targets normally while any target changed after scan start keeps the newer live state.

v3.6.31 historical SAB probe quieting, v3.6.30 runtime-auth/no-op synchronization, v3.6.29 persistent HTTP/1.1 control transport, and v3.6.28 Downloads visibility continuity are unchanged except for the required v3.6.32 adapter identity marker.
name: Automation Target Integrity & Downgrade Protection
